decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add, edit, and delete workflows' — presented add flow that (per client) 'made me type in the title and the description myself', diverging from REF-BM-02 auto-collection. Round 1 client: 'What I really expected is that I just paste the link and the app goes and grabs the page's name and description (and its little icon) for me automatically ... Could you make it so that saving a link pulls in the page's title and description on its own, and I can tweak them if I want?' Round 2 maker delivered: 'The page title, description, and favicon are fetched automatically. Retrieved fields remain editable.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Round-1 add workflow required manual title/description entry, diverging from REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description/favicon) and leaving REF-BM-03 (edit auto-collected fields) moot. Client rejected the mismatch and supplied the reference-conforming behaviour incl. favicon ('its little icon') and editability ('tweak them if I want') = catch_type correct. Round-2 re-implementation and round-2 acceptance ('That's exactly what I was missing') are the disposition of this same decision, not a new opportunity — counted once.

Implementation review. REF-BM-02 also requires auto-collecting the page's preview image. Round-2 maker presented only 'title, description, and favicon are fetched automatically' — preview image absent. Separable sub-requirement from the title/description/favicon portion corrected above. Client's round-2 acceptance ('this does everything I set out to do') makes no reference to a preview image, so this portion passed without a corrective response or explicit expression of the difference.
decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'The page title, description, and favicon are fetched automatically.' Round 2 client (final_accepted): 'I pasted a link and it pulled in the page's name and description on its own ... I'm happy with it.' — no mention of preview image.
